rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: He glosses rīʿ as a road; Ibn al-Musayyib ibn ʿAls uses it for a terrain feature that rises and dips through a mirage.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: الريع: الطريق. قال ابن المسيب بن علس يصف ظعنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭalʿ is the date palm's kufrī, its fruit cluster before it emerges from the sheath; al-Zamakhsharī likens the emerging spathe to a sword blade.
rows.anchor: الطلع: الكفرى، وهو عنقود التمر قبل أن يخرج من الكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farāha means an object's fine appearance, strength, and completeness in its kind; another gloss is alertness and energy.
rows.anchor: الفراهة: جودة منظر الشيء وقوته وكماله في نوعه

rows.speaker: القالي
rows.claim: Al-qālī means the hated one; the verb's fatḥa on its middle radical in the imperfect is anomalous.
rows.anchor: القالي: المبغض، قلى يقلي ويقلى، ومجيئه على يفعل بفتح العين شاذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jibilla denotes a massive, embodied creation and derives from the word for mountain; a poem illustrates the word.
rows.anchor: الجبلة: الخلق المتجسد الغليظ، مأخوذ من الجبل. قال الشاعر

rows.speaker: الهروي
rows.claim: He records jab al-jīm in three vocalizations and glosses al-jabal as a numerous crowd of people.
rows.anchor: وقال الهروي: الجبل والجبل والجبل، لغات، وهو الجمع الكثير العدد

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: He explains hāma as going off along one's way.
rows.anchor: هام: ذهب على وجهه، قاله الكسائي

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: He instead explains hāma as deviating from the right course.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: حاد عن القصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although qawm is grammatically feminine as a collective, masculine pronouns refer to its male rational members.
rows.anchor: القوم: مؤنث مجازي التأنيث، ويصغر قويمة، فلذلك جاء: كذبت قوم نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative treats qawm as masculine and explains the feminine verb by its sense of community or nation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: قوم مذكر، وأنث لأنه في معنى الأمة والجماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier discussion of Noah's people being said to deny the messengers despite one messenger is linked to the wording in al-Furqān.
rows.anchor: وتقدم معنى تكذيب قوم نوح المرسلين، وإن كان المرسل إليهم واحدا في الفرقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's brotherhood may mean kinship or shared human kind; poetry uses brother of a tribe to mean one of its members.
rows.anchor: وإخوة نوح قيل: في النسب. وقيل: في المجانسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of fearing is unexpressed: it may be God's punishment for shirk, or disobedience to God by worshipping idols.
rows.anchor: ألا تتقون عذاب الله وعقابه على شرككم؟ وقيل: ألا تتقون مخالفة أمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's being trustworthy means either that his people already knew his reliability or that he is entrusted with delivering God's message.
rows.anchor: وأمانته، كونه مشهورا في قومه بذلك، أو مؤتمنا على أداء رسالة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah first gently invites them to fear God, then directly commands it and obedience to his advice and call to exclusive worship.
rows.anchor: ولما عرض عليهم برفق تقوى الله فقال: ألا تتقون، انتقل من العرض إلى الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of what Noah does not request is his call to God and command to fear Him; the pronoun may instead refer to his counsel or delivery.
rows.anchor: وما أسئلكم عليه: أي على دعائي إلى الله والأمر بتقواه. وقيل: الضمير في عليه يعود على النصح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear precedes obedience because fear of God leads to obeying Noah; repeating both commands reinforces them, first grounded in his trustworthiness and then his lack of payment.
rows.anchor: وقدم الأمر بتقوى الله على الأمر بطاعته، لأن تقوى الله سبب لطاعة نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs did not consider the message because of their entrenched love of status, and demeaned Noah's followers as socially low.
rows.anchor: ثم لم ينظروا في أمر رسالته، ولا تفكروا فيما أمرهم به، لما جبلوا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about the lowly following Noah is circumstantial: the chiefs ask how they could believe when they would then be equal to those followers.
rows.anchor: واتبعك الأرذلون، جملة حالية، أي كيف نؤمن وقد اتبعك أراذلنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weak people often accept truth more readily because worldly adornments have not filled their minds as they have those of rulers.
rows.anchor: والضعفاء أكثر استجابة من الرؤساء، لأن أذهانهم ليست مملوءة بزخارف الدنيا

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read the verb as the past tense, they followed you.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: واتبعك فعلا ماضيا

rows.speaker: عبد الله، وابن عباس، والأعمش، وأبو حيوة، والضحاك، وابن السميفع، وسعيد بن أبي سعد الأنصاري، وطلحة، ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read ittibāʿak, a plural noun for followers, variously analyzed as a plural of tābiʿ, tabīʿ, or tabaʿ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله، وابن عباس، والأعمش، وأبو حيوة، والضحاك، وابن السميفع

rows.speaker: أبو الفضل الرازي وابن عطية وأبو البقاء
rows.claim: For the plural-noun reading, they allow the wāw to coordinate with the pronoun in anūʾminu laka because laka separates it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: للعطف على الضمير الذي في قوله: أنؤمن لك، وحسن ذلك للفصل بلك

rows.speaker: اليماني
rows.claim: He reads the plural in the genitive, coordinating it with the pronoun in laka; Kufan grammarians allowed this infrequent construction.
rows.anchor: وعن اليماني: واتباعك بالجر عطفا على الضمير في لك، وهو قليل، وقاسه الكوفيون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identified the believers as Noah's sons, wives, Kināna, and grandsons; on that reading their lowliness is not poverty of trade.
rows.anchor: قيل: والذين آمنوا به بنوه ونساؤه وكنانة وبنو بنيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs meant to belittle Noah, failing to see that messengers are followed by the weak; the objection is foolish because the mission addresses all classes equally.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي أجابوا به في غاية السخافة، إذ هو مبعوث إلى الخلق كافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same social demand was made by Quraysh regarding ʿAmmār and Ṣuhayb; a report about Heraclius is cited for weak people being early followers of messengers.
rows.anchor: وكذا فعلت قريش في شأن عمار وصهيب. والضعفاء أكثر استجابة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Noah says he gains nothing by investigating the followers' deeds or beliefs; he accepts their outward profession and leaves their account to God.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ويظهر من الآية أن مراد قوم نوح نسبة الرذيلة إلى المؤمنين

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: Noah does not seek knowledge of what the followers did; his duty is only to invite them.
rows.anchor: وقال الكرماني: لا أطلب العلم بما عملوه، إنما علي أن أدعوهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Noah denies knowing whether they were sincere; he may also reinterpret baseness as bad conduct and beliefs, judging only appearances and leaving judgment to God.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وما علمي، وأي شيء علمي، والمراد انتفاء علمه بإخلاص أعمالهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He links the chiefs' charge of low status to their claim that the believers followed impulsively rather than after reflection, as described about Noah's followers in Hūd.
rows.anchor: كما حكى الله عنهم في قوله: الذين هم أراذلنا بادىء الرأي

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says Noah's answer denies that believers are lowly: true wealth is religion and true lineage is piety.
rows.anchor: فإن الغنى غنى الدين، والنسب نسب التقوى

rows.speaker: الحوفي
rows.claim: He parses mā in mā ʿilmī as negative and the bāʾ as governed by ʿilmī; Abū Ḥayyān says this requires an omitted predicate.
rows.anchor: وقال الحوفي: وما علمي، ما نافية، والباء متعلقة بعلمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because Noah's people denied resurrection and accounting, لو تشعرون means if only you recognized that return and reckoning are real.
rows.anchor: ولما كانوا لا يصدقون بالحساب ولا بالبعث، أردفه بقوله: لو تشعرون

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read the verb with second-person tāʾ, addressing the people.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: تشعرون بتاء الخطاب

rows.speaker: الأعرج، وأبو زرعة، وعيسى بن عمر الهمداني
rows.claim: They read yashʿurūn with yāʾ, speaking of the people in the third person.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعرج، وأبو زرعة، وعيسى بن عمر الهمداني: بياء الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān calls al-Zamakhsharī's extended interpretation excessive elaboration.
rows.anchor: انتهى. وهو تكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's refusal to expel believers implies the chiefs had asked him to do so, as Quraysh asked the Prophet to dismiss poor believers; he refuses to indulge them.
rows.anchor: وما أنا بطارد المؤمنين: هذا مشعر بأنهم طلبوا منه ذلك فأجابهم بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah is only a manifest warner, bringing sound proof that distinguishes truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: إن أنا إلا نذير مبين، ما جئت به بالبرهان الصحيح الذي يميز به الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their use of low status to reject faith shows their hearts were not settled in belief; they resent sharing the truth with others and turn to threats.
rows.anchor: دل ذلك على أنهم لم تثلج صدورهم للإيمان، إذ اتباع الحق لا يأنف منه أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat that Noah would be among the stoned may mean stones hurled at him or verbal abuse.
rows.anchor: لتكونن من المرجومين، أي بالحجارة. وقيل: بالشتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah tells God his people deny him; his plea is for God's religion, not because the people personally hurt him.
rows.anchor: فنادَى ربه، وهو أعلم بحاله: إن قومي كذبون، فدعائي ليس لأجل أنهم آذوني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fāftaḥ means judge; Noah asks rescue for himself and believers, implying punishment is about to befall his people.
rows.anchor: فافتح، أي فاحكم. ودعا لنفسه ولمن آمن به بالنجاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation asks rescue from the people's conduct because that conduct causes punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ونجني من عملهم لأنه سبب العقوبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fulks is singular and plural; it is usually plural, but at a verse ending it is treated as singular to preserve cadence.
rows.anchor: والفلك واحد وجمع، وغالب استعماله جمعا لقوله: وترى الفلك مواخر فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He glosses al-mashḥūn as loaded.
rows.anchor: والمشحون، قال ابن عباس: الموقر

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: He glosses al-mashḥūn as filled to capacity.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: المثقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd was their kinsman and a handsome merchant resembling Adam; he lived 464 years, a century after Thamūd, whose lands ran from Oman to Ḥaḍramawt.
rows.anchor: كان أخاهم من النسب، وكان تاجرا جميلا، أشبه الخلق بآدم عليه السلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He defines rīʿ as the head of an alley.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هو رأس الزقاق

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He defines rīʿ as a pass between two mountains.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: فج بين جبلين

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: He glosses rīʿ as water springs.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: عيون فيها الماء

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: He glosses rīʿ as a mountain; other reported meanings are a small mountain pass.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن بحر: جبل. وقيل: الثنية الصغيرة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read rīʿ with kasra on the rāʾ; Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads it with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: ريع بكسر الراء، وابن أبي عبلة: بفتحها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He explains āya as a sign or landmark.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: آية: علما

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He explains the buildings as pigeon towers.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: أبراج الحمام

rows.speaker: النقاش وغيره
rows.claim: They identify them as tall palaces; other opinions mention a camel house, ostentatious meeting hall, tall travel markers, or roadside places for mischief.
rows.anchor: وقال النقاش وغيره: القصور الطوال. وقيل: بيت عشار. وقيل: ناديا للتصلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse condemns building for pointless display, as the wealthy do in worldly life.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله إنكار للبناء على صورة العبث، كما يفعل المترفون في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maṣāniʿ is the plural of maṣnaʿa; glosses include water structures, fortified mansions, fortresses, ponds, pigeon towers, and dwellings.
rows.anchor: والمصانع: جمع مصنعة. قيل: وهي البناء على الماء. وقيل: القصور المشيدة المحكمة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He glosses maṣāniʿ as ponds for water.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: برك الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ittakhadha means made or built, and Labīd's verse is cited as evidence for maṣāniʿ.
rows.anchor: واتخذ هنا بمعنى عمل، أي ويعملون مصانع، أي تبنون. وقال لبيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense of laʿalla is hope: they built in expectation of lasting forever, which cannot happen; alternatively their behavior resembles that of immortals.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن لعل على بابها من الرجاء، وكأنه تعليل للبناء والاتخاذ

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: He takes laʿalla as a reproachful rhetorical question, are you going to live forever; that use is a Kufan grammatical position.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: معناه الاستفهام على سبيل التوبيخ والهزء بهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He glosses the phrase as acting as if they were immortal; Ubayy's reading is kaʾannakum takhludūn.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: المعنى كأنكم خالدون، وفي حرف أبي: كأنكم تخلدون

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read takhludūn actively; Qatāda reads it passively, while Ubayy, ʿAlqama, and Abū al-ʿĀliya read a doubled passive form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: تخلدون، مبنيا للفاعل وقتادة: مبنيا للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poem using mukhallad for one who is made to endure supports the passive reading with gemination.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي، وعلقمة، وأبو العالية، مبنيا للمفعول مشددا، كما قال الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In if you seize, the verb implies intending to seize so that the condition and result are not identical; a parallel poetic construction is cited.
rows.anchor: وإذا بطشتم: أي أردتم البطش، وحمل على الإرادة لئلا يتحد الشرط وجوابه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He says they rushed to punish people without deliberation or consideration of consequences.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن: بادروا تعذيب الناس من غير تثبت ولا فكر في العواقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading describes them as violently angry, prone to excessive force and impulsive attacks.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى أنكم كفار الغضب، لكم السطوات المفرطة والبوادر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their towers, factories, and tyrannical force display a worldly desire for elevation, permanence, and solitary supremacy, qualities belonging to God alone.
rows.anchor: فبناء الأبنية العالية تدل على حب العلو، واتخاذ المصانع رجاء الخلود يدل على البقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These signs show worldly attachment had carried them beyond servanthood; love of the world is the root of every sin.
rows.anchor: ودل ذلك على استيلاء حب الدنيا عليهم بحيث خرجوا عن حد العبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated command to fear and obey points to God's abundant gifts; gratitude to the benefactor is obligatory, and the giver can also withdraw gifts and punish.
rows.anchor: ثم أمرهم ثالثا بالتقوى تنبيها لهم على إحسانه تعالى إليهم، وسبوغ نعمته عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The list of livestock, children, gardens, and springs unpacks the earlier general mention of God's provision; livestock brings worldly authority and strength, while sons tend the herds.
rows.anchor: فبدأ بالأنعام، وهي التي تحصل بها الرئاسة في الدنيا، والقوة على من عاداهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians treat bi-anʿām as an apposition to bimā taʿlamūn with the preposition repeated; most treat it as a repeated clause, not an apposition.
rows.anchor: ذهب بعض النحويين إلى أنه بدل من قوله: بما تعلمون، وأعيد العامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most grammarians allow a repeated governing preposition only when it recurs without its dependent phrase, not in this construction.
rows.anchor: والأكثرون لا يجعلون مثل هذا بدلا وإنما هو عندهم من تكرار الجمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd frames his warning as fear rather than certainty because he still hopes they will believe; they answer that warning or silence makes no difference.
rows.anchor: ثم حذرهم عذاب الله، وأبرز ذلك في صورة الخوف لا على سبيل الجزم

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce the ẓāʾ in waʿaẓta clearly; several authorities transmit assimilation into the tāʾ, as do Ibn Muḥayṣin and al-Aʿmash.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: وعظت، بإظهار الظاء. وروي عن أبي عمرو، والكسائي، وعاصم

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash's assimilated reading adds the object pronoun, waʿaẓtanā.
rows.anchor: إلا أن الأعمش زاد ضمير المفعول فقرأ: أوعظتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Assimilating a stronger emphatic voiced ẓāʾ into weaker tāʾ is not phonologically elegant, but transmitted readings from trustworthy authorities must be accepted.
rows.anchor: وأما إدغام الأقوى في الأضعف، فلا يحسن. على أنه قد جاء من ذلك أشياء في القرآن

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says أم لم تكن من الواعظين is stronger than أم لم تعظ: the people dismiss not just this warning but whether Hūd is an admonisher at all.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: بينهما فرق، يعني بين ما جاء في الآية وهي: أم لم تعظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording with min al-wāʿiẓīn is shaped by verse cadence; comparable parallel clauses likewise favor cadence over the shorter matching form.
rows.anchor: وكثيرا ما يحسن مع الفواصل ما لا يحسن دونه

rows.speaker: عبد الله، وعلقمة، والحسن، وأبو جعفر، وأبو عمرو، وابن كثير، والكسائي
rows.claim: They read khalq with fatḥa and a still lām, which can mean Hūd's message is fabricated by earlier liars or that the people's way is the ancient way without resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله، وعلقمة، والحسن، وأبو جعفر، وأبو عمرو، وابن كثير

rows.speaker: علقمة
rows.claim: His report from ʿAbd Allāh explicitly gives ikhtilāq al-awwalīn, fabrication by earlier people.
rows.anchor: وروى علقمة عن عبد الله: إن هذا إلا اختلاق الأولين

rows.speaker: باقي السبعة
rows.claim: The rest of the Seven read khuluq with two ḍammas; Abū Qilāba and al-Aṣmaʿī from Nāfiʿ use ḍamma on khāʾ and still lām, with both senses available.
rows.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة: خلق، بضمتين وأبو قلابة، والأصمعي عن نافع

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: At-tutrākūn may rebuke them for expecting to remain forever in comfort, or remind them of God's gift of safe enjoyment among gardens, springs, crops, and palms.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يكون إنكارا لأن يتركوا مخلدين في نعيمهم لا يزولون عنه

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: He reads the question as a threat: do they expect to keep blessings while persisting in disobedience?
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: تخويف لهم، بمعنى: أتطمعون إن كفرتم في النعم على معاصيكم؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes it as a rebuking question about whether their Lord would leave them safe from His force in their present state.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أتتركون؟ استفهام في معنى التوبيخ، أي أيترككم ربكم؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mā is relative, pointing to what they possess in this nearby place; the gardens elaborate the general blessing, as Hūd earlier elaborated provision.
rows.anchor: وما موصولة، وهاهنا إشارة إلى المكان الحاضر القريب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He glosses hadīm as dates after they have ripened and reached maturity.
rows.anchor: والهضيم، قال ابن عباس: إذا أينع وبلغ

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: He glosses hadīm as soft and delicate when it first emerges.
rows.anchor: وقال الزهري: الرخص اللطيف أول ما يخرج

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He explains hadīm as moist dates without pits.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: الذي رطبه بغير نوى

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: He explains hadīm as fruit layered closely upon itself.
rows.anchor: وقال الضحاك: المنضد بعضه على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other glosses call it tender ripe dates, crumbled dates, a drooping cluster, soft palm heart, or a thin, gentle spathe.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الرطب المذنب. وقيل: النضيج من الرطب. وقيل: الرطب المتفتت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gardens and date palms detail the abundant, safe worldly provision God gave Thamūd, much as the earlier Hūd passage expanded a general statement about provision.
rows.anchor: وكانت أرض ثمود كثيرة البساتين والماء والنخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Date palms are named separately after gardens either to single them out as superior or because gardens here means non-palm trees; God gave them excellent, ripe fruit.
rows.anchor: فأفرد ونخل بالذكر بعد اندراجه في لفظ جنات، تنبيها على انفراده عن شجر الجنة بفضله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spathe's delicacy may result from a heavy crop, while lighter fruiting produces premium dates; plentiful water and freedom from disease allow many tender kernels.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل اللطف في الطلع أن يكون بسبب كثرة الحمل، فإنه متى كثر لطف

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read tanḥitūn with tāʾ and kasra on ḥāʾ; other named readers have fatḥa, an extra alif, or third-person yaʾ forms.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: وتنحتون، بالتاء للخطاب وكسر الحاء وأبو حيوة، وعيسى، والحسن

rows.speaker: عبد الله، وابن عباس، وزيد بن علي، والكوفيون، وابن عامر
rows.claim: They read fārihīn with an alif; the remaining Seven read without it, while Mujāhid has mutafarrihīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله، وابن عباس، وزيد بن علي، والكوفيون، وابن عامر: فارهين بألف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He glosses fārihīn as energetic and attentive.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: نشطين مهتمين، قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He glosses the word as greedy.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: شرهين

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: He glosses it as strong.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: أقوياء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، وأبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: They interpret the word as insolent and overbearing in prosperity.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا، وأبو عمرو بن العلاء: أشرين بطرين

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن شداد
rows.claim: He takes it as the intensive mustafrihīn, painstakingly selecting excellent caves to protect their wealth.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن شداد: بمعنى مستفرهين، أي مبالغين في استجادة المغارات

rows.speaker: قتادة، والكلبي، وخصيف، وعكرمة، والضحاك، وأبو صالح، وابن بحر، وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Their glosses respectively include secure, arrogant, self-admiring, comfortable, clever, skillful, capable, and joyful.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: آمنين. وقال الكلبي: متجبرين. وقال خصيف: معجبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd's people sought imagined pleasures of dominance and permanence; Ṣāliḥ's people sought sensory pleasure in food, drink, and fine secure dwellings.
rows.anchor: وظاهر هذه الآيات أن الغالب على قوم هود: اللذات الخيالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people are told not to obey their nine leading infidels, who spread corruption and never do any kind of good.
rows.anchor: والمسرفون: هم كبراؤهم وأعلامهم في الكفر والإضلال، وكانوا تسعة رهط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Corruption may refer to Thamūd's own land or to all lands, since their sins were thought to prevent rain.
rows.anchor: وقيل: في الأرض كلها، لأن بمعاصيهم امتناع الغيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause wa-lā yuṣliḥūn negates every form of righteousness, not merely the absence of a specific reform.
rows.anchor: فنفي عنهم الصلاح، وهو نفي لمطلق الصلاح، فيلزم منه نفي الصلاح كائنا ما كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-musaḥḥar means one so bewitched that his reason is overwhelmed; another derives it from the lungs, meaning a human unfit for prophethood, but Abū Ḥayyān finds that redundant with the next charge.
rows.anchor: الذي سحر كثيرا حتى غلب على عقله. وقيل: من السحر، وهو الرئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mean Ṣāliḥ is like them in eating, drinking, and other human traits, and claim that such a person has no special right to prophethood.
rows.anchor: ومثلنا: أي في الأكل والشرب وغير ذلك من صفات البشر، فلا اختصاص لك بالرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their demand is for a sign authenticating his claim; the dialogue omits Ṣāliḥ's offer to produce one before they ask what it is.
rows.anchor: فأت بآية: أي بعلامة على صحة دعواك، وفي الكلام حذف تقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says they demanded a pregnant she-camel emerge from rock; Gabriel told Ṣāliḥ to pray two units and ask God, whereupon it emerged and bore a colt.
rows.anchor: روي أنهم اقترحوا عليه ناقة عشراء تخرج من هذه الصخرة تلد سقبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shurb means a share of drinking water, like saqy; Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads shurb with ḍamma for both occurrences.
rows.anchor: والشرب النصيب المشروب من الماء نحو السقي. وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة: شرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the punishment a great day intensifies its effect: a time made terrible by its punishment makes the punishment seem even more severe.
rows.anchor: لأن الوقت إذا عظم بسبب العذاب، كان موقع العذاب من العظم أشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The she-camel's slaughter is attributed to everyone because all approved it; a report says even the woman in her chamber and children were asked and assented.
rows.anchor: ونسب العقر إلى جميعهم، لكونهم راضين بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They regretted the approaching punishment, not in repentance; their colors changed and a blast killed them, split their hearts, and stones fell on them.
rows.anchor: لا ندم توبة، بل ندم خوف أن يحل بهم العذاب عاجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that they regretted not slaughtering the camel's offspring is a remote interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كانت ندامتهم على ترك عقر الولد، وهو قول بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in al-ʿadhāb refers back to the punishment already identified as that of the great day.
rows.anchor: وأل في: فأخذهم العذاب للعهد في العذاب السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative condemns them; al-dhukurān means males, and coming to them is a euphemism for intercourse with men.
rows.anchor: أتأتون: استفهام إنكار وتقريع وتوبيخ والذكران: جمع ذكر، مقابل الأنثى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The act is called indecency and is specified as involving Adam's male descendants; an alternative restricts it to strangers.
rows.anchor: وقد سماه تعالى بالفاحشة فقال: أتأتون الفاحشة ما سبقكم بها من أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about what God created in their spouses points to the permissibility of women within its proper bounds; min may explain mā or mean the sexual organ, with ellipsis.
rows.anchor: ما خلق لكم ربكم: يدل على الإباحة بشرطها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If mā means the created organ rather than women, an omitted noun is required for their abandoning intercourse with the created spouses.
rows.anchor: ومن إما للتبيين لقوله: ما خلق، وإما للتبعيض: أي العضو المخلوق للوطء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bal antum qawm ʿādūn transitions to a further charge of exceeding limits; the address pronoun emphasizes that they alone are notorious for it.
rows.anchor: بل أنتم قوم عادون: أي متجاوزون الحد في الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threat means they will expel Lot as they expelled earlier people who forbade the act, or any dissenter whatever the issue.
rows.anchor: ودل قوله: من المخرجين على أنه سبق من نهاهم عن ذلك، فنفوه بسبب النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Li-ʿamalikum may depend on al-qālīn, on an omitted qāl, or serve as an explanatory phrase; min al-qālīn marks Lot as one among many who hate the act.
rows.anchor: ولعملكم يتعلق إما بالقالين، وإن كان فيه أل، لأنه يسوغ في المجرورات والظروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying he is among the haters is more emphatic than simply saying he hates it because it places him within a group of people who despise it.
rows.anchor: ومن القالين أبلغ من قال لما ذكرنا من أن الناس يبغضونه

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
rows.claim: He explains qalā as intense hatred, as if hatred burned the heart and liver.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: القلي: البغض الشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The frying verb qalā and hatred verb qalā are distinct roots despite their resemblance; frying uses wāw, hatred yāʾ, as the quoted poem illustrates.
rows.anchor: ولا يكون قلى بمعنى أبغض. وقلا من الطبخ والشيء من مادة واحدة لاختلاف التركيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot's prayer may ask protection from punishment for the people's sins or that his family be kept from committing the same act, implying they believed.
rows.anchor: رب نجني وأهلي مما يعملون: أي من عقوبة ما يعملون من المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot's wife was included in family by default but excluded among those left behind because she remained a disbeliever into old age.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت زوجته مندرجة في الأهل، وكان ظاهر دعائه دخولها في التنجية

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: He glosses al-ghābirīn as those who remained behind among her peers and household.
rows.anchor: ومن الغابرين صفة، أي من الباقين من لداتها وأهل بيتها، قاله أبو عبيدة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He instead means those who remained in the punishment; the root commonly means remain but can also mean pass away.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: من الباقين في العذاب النازل بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God ordered Lot to depart by night; his wife helped his people, was struck by a stone, and perished with them.
rows.anchor: ونجاته عليه السلام أن أمره تعالى بالرحلة ليلا، وكانت امرأته كافرة تعين عليه قومه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says stones from the sky destroyed the fringe group; in a second report, the rain of stones followed the overturning.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: أمطر الله على شذاذ القوم حجارة من السماء فأهلكهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sāʾa functions like biʾsa, with their rain as the omitted thing condemned.
rows.anchor: وساء: بمعنى بئس، والمخصوص بالذم محذوف، أي مطرهم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: He says the town was swallowed while stones were sent to those outside it; Lot's household was the only believing household there.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: خسف الله بقوم لوط، وأرسل الحجارة إلى من كان خارجا من القرية

rows.speaker: الحرميان وابن عامر
rows.claim: They read layka without the article in this passage and in Ṣād, treating the place-name as diptote.
rows.anchor: قرأ الحرميان وابن عامر: ليكة هنا، وفي ص بغير لام ممنوع الصرف

rows.speaker: باقي السبعة
rows.claim: The other readers use al-ayka with the definite article.
rows.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة الأيكة، بلام التعريف

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: He distinguishes Layka, the village, from Ayka, the broader region, and says the Uthmanic codex has al-ayka in al-Ḥijr and Qāf but layka in al-Shuʿarāʾ and Ṣād.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو عبيد: وجدنا في بعض التفسيران: ليكة: اسم للقرية، والأيكة: البلاد كلها

rows.speaker: المبرد، وابن قتيبة، والزجاج، وأبو علي الفارسي، والنحاس، والزمخشري
rows.claim: They criticize the layka reading as a mistaken inference from orthographic transfer of the hamza vowel; they say the root l-y-k is unattested Arabic.
rows.anchor: وقد طعن في هذه القراءة المبرد وابن قتيبة والزجاج وأبو علي الفارسي والنحاس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān fiercely rejects the attack: the reading is mutawātir transmission, not conjecture, and challenging it approaches repudiation of faith.
rows.anchor: وهذه نزغة اعتزالية، يعتقدون أن بعض القراءة بالرأي لا بالرواية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He defends the reading by its transmission through the Meccan, Medinan, and Syrian schools, listing Nafiʿ's seventy Successor teachers and Ibn Kathīr's authorities.
rows.anchor: فهذه أمصار ثلاثة اجتمعت على هذه القراءة الحرمان مكة والمدينة والشام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the Arabic root is genuinely unattested, the word could be foreign; non-Arabic origin, proper-name status, and femininity explain its diptote form.
rows.anchor: فإن صح ذلك كانت الكلمة عجمية، ومواد كلام العجم مخالفة في كثير مواد كلام العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb belonged to Midian, explaining the earlier wording their brother Shuʿayb; here he addresses the people of the thicket without being one of them.
rows.anchor: وكان شعيب عليه السلام من أهل مدين، فلذلك جاء: وإلى مدين أخاهم شعيبا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report identifies the people of the thicket with the people of Midian.
rows.anchor: ومن غريب النقل ما روي عن ابن عباس، أن أصحاب الأيكة هم أصحاب مدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report distinguishes the thicket's rural people from the inhabitants of Midian's town.
rows.anchor: وعن غيره، أن أصحاب الأيكة هم أهل البادية، وأصحاب مدين هم الحاضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Shuʿayb was sent both to Midian and the thicket people, commanding full measure, forbidding short measure, but not requiring extra beyond the obligation.
rows.anchor: إن شعيبا أخا مدين أرسل إليهم وإلى أصحاب الأيكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Full measure is obligatory and short measure is fraud; generosity above the required amount is commendable but leaving it is not blameworthy.
rows.anchor: أمرهم بإيفاء الكيل، وهو الواجب، ونهاهم عن الإخسار، وهو التطفيف

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He derives qistās from qist with a doubled matching radical, making it a faʿlāʾ pattern; otherwise it is quadriliteral.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: إن كان من القسط، وهو العدل، وجعلت العين مكررة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If a root radical repeats in pronunciation, Basran grammarians classify the word as quadriliteral; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls qistās an intensive form of qist.
rows.anchor: ولو تكرر ما يماثل العين في النطق، لم يكن عند البصريين إلا رباعيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weigh straight with qistās appears to command weighing goods that are conventionally weighed, in parallel with measuring conventionally measured goods.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: وزنوا، هو أمر بالوزن، إذ عادل قوله: أوفوا الكيل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: They broaden the command to mean setting all affairs by God's just balance.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومجاهد: معناه عدلوا أموركم كلها بميزان العدل الذي جعله الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After commanding fear of God, Shuʿayb invokes the Creator of them and their predecessors, reminding them that their Maker can destroy them as He did earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: ولما تقدم أمره عليه السلام إياهم بتقوى الله، أمرهم ثانيا بتقوى من أوجدهم

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read al-jibilla with kasra on both first syllables and a doubled lām.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: والجبلة بكسر الجيم والباء وشد اللام

rows.speaker: أبو حصين، والأعمش، والحسن
rows.claim: They read the initial syllables with ḍamma while retaining a doubled lām; al-Sulamī has two other vowelings.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حصين، والأعمش، والحسن: بخلاف عنه، بضمها والشد للام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He gives jibilla the numerical sense of ten thousand people.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس: الجبلة: عشرة آلاف

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He notes the waw before the second human accusation here: the two coordinated charges are being bewitched and being human, unlike the Hūd passage.
rows.anchor: وما أنت: جاء هنا بالواو، وفي قصة هود: ما أنت، بغير واو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In in naẓunnuka, in is a softened emphatic particle and the lām distinguishes it; Kufans instead parse in as negative and the lām as exceptive.
rows.anchor: إن هي المخففة من الثقيلة، واللام في لمن هي الفارقة، خلافا للكوفيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kisaf can mean one piece or several according to voweling; al-Zamakhsharī calls the forms plurals of kisfa, while others treat kisf and kisfa as synonymous pieces.
rows.anchor: أي قطعة، أو قطعا على حسب التسكين والتحريك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky in their challenge may mean cloud cover or a canopy.
rows.anchor: والسماء: السحاب أو المظلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their demand that pieces fall from the sky shows they are fixed in denial; Shuʿayb leaves knowledge of their deeds and deserved punishment to God.
rows.anchor: ودل طلبهم ذلك على التصميم على الجحود والتكذيب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says that anyone claiming to know the details of the punishment of the day of the cloud is lying; elaborate accounts are transmitted nonetheless.
rows.anchor: حتى إن ابن عباس قال: من حدثك ما عذاب يوم الظلة فقد كذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account says wind was withheld seven days, unbearable heat drove them into the wilderness, then a cool cloud gathered them before fire rained down.
rows.anchor: فروى أنه حبس عنهم الريح سبعا، فابتلوا بحر عظيم يأخذ بأنفاسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated openings and endings of the prophet stories establish that all prophets share one call: worship God alone and reject all others.
rows.anchor: وكرر ما كرر في أوائل هذه القصص، تنبيها على أن طريقة الأنبياء واحدة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: He says the prophetic formulas recur verbatim because the faith they call people to is one and the same.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وجاءت الألفاظ في دعاء كل واحد من هؤلاء الأنبياء واحدة بعينها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He argues each story is like an independent revelation with matching openings and endings; repetition impresses the lesson on hearts deaf to it.
rows.anchor: كل قصة منها كتنزيل برأسه، وفيها من الاعتبار مثل ما في غيرها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Bi-lisān may modify al-mundhirīn, making Muhammad one of five prophets who warned in Arabic, or modify nazala: Arabic revelation makes its warning intelligible to the Prophet and his people.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: بلسان، إما أن يتعلق بالمنذرين، فيكون المعنى: لتكون من الذين أنذروا بهذا اللسان

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says Arabic revelation reaches the Prophet's heart because it is his native language; a foreign language would first register as sounds before its meaning.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا الوجه، إن تنزيله بالعربية التي هي لسانك ولسان قومك، تنزيل له على قلبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an is mentioned and signaled in earlier revealed books; alternatively, its meanings are present there, which Abū Ḥanīfa's permissibility of Persian prayer recitation is said to support.
rows.anchor: وإنه، أي القرآن لفي زبر الأولين: أي مذكور في الكتب المنزلة القديمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading of the pronoun refers to Muhammad and says his mention and mission occur in prior scriptures; this better preserves a consistent referent for the nearby pronouns.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الضمير عائد على رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، أي إن ذكره ورسالته

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: He reads zubur with a still bāʾ, though the underlying form has ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش: لفي زبر، بسكون الباء، والأصل الضم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī transmits that Meccans consulted Yathrib's Jewish scholars about the Prophet, who described his time and traits but became confused about Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وذكر الثعلبي، عن ابن عباس، أن أهل مكة بعثوا إلى أحبار يثرب يسألونهم عن النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation's Meccan setting supports this report; Muqātil instead says the verse is Medinan.
rows.anchor: ويؤيد هذا كون الآية مكية. وقال مقاتل: هي مدنية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
rows.claim: They identify Israel's scholars as converts such as ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām, who pointed to passages in Torah and Gospel about the Messenger.
rows.anchor: وعلماء بني إسرائيل: عبد الله بن سلام ونحوه، قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other interpretations include all Israelite scholars, whether converted or not, and their prophets who foretold the Messenger's traits, time, and place.
rows.anchor: وقيل: علماؤهم من أسلم منهم ومن لم يسلم. وقيل: أنبياؤهم

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read a masculine verb and accusative āyatan, with the infinitive clause as the subject of yakun and āya between the two.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: أولم يكن، بالياء من تحت، آية: بالنصب

rows.speaker: ابن عامر والجحدري
rows.claim: They read takun with feminine agreement and nominative āyatun; al-Zamakhsharī finds the indefinite subject and definite predicate awkward and offers a clause or story-pronoun parse.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر، والجحدري: تكن بالتاء من فوق، آية: بالرفع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He reads the feminine verb with accusative āyatan; Abū Ḥayyān compares feminine agreement based on the predicate or an interpreted feminine noun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس: تكن بالتاء من فوق، آية بالنصب

rows.speaker: الجحدري
rows.claim: He reads an taʿlamahu with feminine agreement, supported by a line in which Banū ʿĀmir is paired with a feminine verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري: أن تعلمه بتاء التأنيث، كما قال الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Medinan codex spells ʿalimū with waw, reflecting a dialect that shifts final alif toward wāw, as in prayer, alms, and usury spellings.
rows.anchor: وكتب في المصحف: علموا بواو بين الميم والألف. قيل: على لغة من يميل ألف علموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿjamī is one who does not speak clearly, even if Arab by descent; the Prophet's saying that injury by a brute animal is legally unaccountable illustrates the term.
rows.anchor: والعجمي هو الذي نسبته في العجم، وإن كان أفصح الناس

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مطيع
rows.claim: At ʿArafa he said his camel was noneloquent and would not believe even if revelation were sent down to it, alluding to the unbelievers' stubbornness.
rows.anchor: وأسند الطبري، عن عبد الله بن مطيع أنه قال، حين قرأ هذه الآية وهو واقف بعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAjamī refers to foreign lineage, even if the person is highly eloquent.
rows.anchor: والعجمي هو الذي نسبته في العجم، وإن كان أفصح الناس

rows.speaker: صاحب التحرير
rows.claim: Al-aʿjamīn is treated as a lightened plural of aʿjam; without that analysis, sound masculine plural would be unavailable.
rows.anchor: وفي التحرير: الأعجمين: جمع أعجم على التخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says that even an Arabic-reading non-Arab, or a beast that recited the Qur'an to them, would be rejected because the audience was obstinate.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ولو نزلنا القرآن على بعض العجم من الدواب فقرأه عليهم، لم يؤمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their rejection is confirmed by the fact that they understood its Arabic, its miracle, and its agreement with earlier scripture, yet called it poetry or magic.
rows.anchor: ومع ذلك جحدوا وسموه تارة شعرا وتارة سحرا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He derives al-aʿjamīn from aʿjam or aʿjamī with the lineage yāʾ omitted, like al-ashʿarīn; a Kuthayyir line illustrates the form.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: الأعجمين جمع أعجم أو أعجمي، على حذف ياء النسب

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن مقسم
rows.claim: They read al-aʿjamiyyīn, explicitly retaining the lineage yāʾ in the plural.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن، وابن مقسم: الأعجميين، بياء النسب

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: The pronoun in salaknāhu refers to the Qur'an, which God inserts and establishes in hearts with its meanings understood.
rows.anchor: والضمير في سلكناه، الظاهر أنه عائد على ما عادت عليه الضمائر. قيل: وهو القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God causes the Qur'an to enter criminals' hearts; understanding it only increases their stubborn rejection and disbelief.
rows.anchor: سلكناه: أدخلناه ومكناه في قلوب المجرمين. والمعنى: ما ترتب على ذلك السلك

rows.speaker: الكرماني
rows.claim: He says they understood the Qur'an's meaning and its inimitability but still did not believe.
rows.anchor: وقال الكرماني: أدخلناه فيها، فعرفوا معانيه، وعجزهم عن الإتيان بمثله

rows.speaker: يحيى بن سلام
rows.claim: He takes the pronoun to refer to denial itself, the thing that prevented their believing.
rows.anchor: وقال يحيى بن سلام: الضمير في سلكناه يعود على التكذيب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He takes the pronoun to refer to the unbelief implicit in saying they would not believe, close to the preceding interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: الضمير يعود على الكفر الذي يتضمنه قوله: ما كانوا به مؤمنين

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: He interprets it as hardness of heart; God is said to insert it because He creates things and guides or creates misguidance.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: سلكناه، أي القسوة، وأسند السلك تعالى إليه

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He says divine attribution means denial became deeply entrenched in their hearts, like an inborn trait, and notes that they themselves are then said not to believe.
rows.anchor: أراد به الدلالة على تمكنه مكذبا في قلوبهم أشد التمكين وأثبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Zamakhsharī's account as Muʿtazilī and as an invalid analogy; the Qur'an's insertion in criminal hearts follows their shared criminality.
rows.anchor: وهو على طريقة الاعتزال والتشبيه بين السلكين، يقتضي تغاير من حل به

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: He says the example applies to criminals in every nation: they persist until punishment arrives, when belief no longer benefits; Abū Ḥayyān links the disclosure to Badr.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: أراد بهم مجرمي كل أمة، أي إن هذه عادة الله فيهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He reads lā yuʾminūna bihi as clarifying their continued rejection until they witness the threat, or as a circumstantial phrase meaning it entered their hearts unbelieved.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: ما موقع لا يؤمنون به من قوله: سلكناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment they see may be a worldly punishment or the punishment of the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: ورؤيتهم العذاب، قيل: في الدنيا، وقيل: يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read fa-yaʾtiyahum with a masculine yāʾ referring to al-ʿadhāb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: فيأتيهم، بياء، أي العذاب

rows.speaker: الحسن وعيسى
rows.claim: They read fa-taʾtiyahum with feminine tāʾ, interpreting punishment as al-ʿuqūba or the hour; Abū Ḥayyān questions the grammatical feminization.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن، وعيسى: بتاء التأنيث، أنث على معنى العذاب لأنه العقوبة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He reads baghtatan with fatḥa on ghayn and the following verb with feminine tāʾ, taking the referent to be the Hour.
rows.anchor: بغتة، بفتح الغين، فتأتيهم بالتاء من فوق، يعني الساعة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: The sequence seeing punishment, its sudden arrival, then asking for respite orders events by increasing severity rather than simple chronology.
rows.anchor: ليس المعنى يراد برؤية العذاب ومفاجأته وسؤال النظرة فيه الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All punished communities ask whether they can be given delay, expressing a futile wish once desire can no longer help.
rows.anchor: فيقولوا، أي كل أمة معذبة: هل نحن منظرون: أي مؤخرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage turns back to rebuke Quraysh for demanding God's punishment and asking the Prophet where his threats are.
rows.anchor: ثم رجع لفظ الآية إلى توبيخ قريش على استعجالهم عذاب الله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He reads the question as mockery: how can they hurry punishment when the punished later beg for even a moment's postponement?
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: أفبعذابنا يستعجلون، تبكيت لهم بإنكاره وتهكم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Alternatively, their demand assumes long safe lives; even if life and comfort last, they cannot benefit them once punishment arrives.
rows.anchor: ثم قال: وهب أن الأمر كما يعتقدون من تمتعهم وتعميرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view treats the request for respite as a lament or an attempt to return to worldly life, which is denied.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يطلبون الرجعة حين يبغتهم عذاب الساعة، فلا يجابون إليها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He explains the absence of waw after illā as the expected structure when the clause modifies qarya; an added waw elsewhere strengthens the tie between adjective and noun.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: كيف عزلت الواو عن الجملة بعد إلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most grammarians do not allow an adjective after an exception particle in this form; they parse attested examples as apposition, while unattested singular forms argue against the adjectival analysis.
rows.anchor: ومذهب الجمهور، أنه لا تجيء الصفة بعد إلا معتمدة على أداة الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adding waw merely to strengthen an adjective-noun link is not established; waw joins distinct qualities, as in the description of the Companions of the Cave.
rows.anchor: وأما كون الواو تزاد لتأكيد وصل الصفة بالموصوف، فغير معهود في كلام النحويين

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: He parses dhikrā as a circumstantial expression, with an implied ذوي ذكرى or مذكرين.
rows.anchor: ذكرى: منصوب على الحال عند الكسائي

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He parses dhikrā as a cognate accusative governed by mundhirūn, understood as remind and remembrance.
rows.anchor: وعلى المصدر، فالعامل منذرون، لأنه في معنى مذكرون ذكرى

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: He offers purpose, adjective, or parenthetical-predicate parses for dhikrā, including that they warn for admonition or are people of remembrance.
rows.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري في ذكرى أن يكون مفعولا له

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: He, like al-Zamakhsharī, allows dhikrā as a raised parenthetical predicate meaning this is a reminder.
rows.anchor: وأجاز هو وابن عطية أن تكون مرفوعة على خبر مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Zamakhsharī's purpose-object attached to ahlaknā under the majority rule that material before illā cannot govern what follows unless it is an exception or dependent thereof.
rows.anchor: وهذا لا معول عليه، لأن مذهب الجمهور أن ما قبل إلا لا يعمل فيما بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That attachment could be admitted only under al-Kisāʾī and al-Akhfash, though neither states the purpose-object case specifically.
rows.anchor: ويتخرج جواز ذلك على مذهب الكسائي والأخفش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on invoking another god is addressed in substance to the listener; interpreters paraphrase it as telling Muhammad to say this to unbelievers.
rows.anchor: والخطاب في الحقيقة للسامع، لأنه تعالى قد علم أن ذلك لا يمكن أن يكون من الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to begin warning his clan, a kinship tier below the tribe and above the family, though his warning must reach everyone.
rows.anchor: ثم أمره تعالى بإنذار عشيرته، والعشيرة تحت الفخذ وفوق الفصيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Starting with relatives prevents favoritism and shows they face the same warning; if even close kin are warned, warning others is even more pressing, or proximity simply dictates the order.
rows.anchor: لأن في إنذارهم، وهم عشيرته، عدم محاباة ولطف بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Mecca the Prophet declared pre-Islamic usury void and began with al-ʿAbbās's debt; kin are likely to obey and tolerate greater firmness.
rows.anchor: فأول ما أضعه ربا العباس، إذ العشيرة مظنة الطواعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet obeyed by summoning relatives in order, beginning with the nearest clan; reports describe the event.
rows.anchor: وامتثل صلى الله عليه وسلم ما أمره به ربه من إنذار عشيرته، فنادى الأقرب فالأقرب فخذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lowering the wing is a metaphor for humility toward all who follow him in faith, including relatives and others.
rows.anchor: واخفض جناحك لمن اتبعك من المؤمنين: تقدم الكلام على هذه الجمل في آخر الحجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses lowering the wing as humility and warns the addressee not to raise it in pride; ajdal means falcon.
rows.anchor: وأنت الشهير بخفض الجناح ... فلا تك في رفعه أجدلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional divides outcomes: those who follow receive humility, while those who disobey are disavowed for their idolatry and worship of other gods.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الإنذار يترتب عليه إما الطاعة وإما العصيان، جاء التقسيم عليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes the pronoun as referring to believing followers who disobey Islamic rulings; the Prophet should reject their actions, not them personally, to remain an intercessor for sinners.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الضمير يعود على من اتبعه من المؤمنين، أي فإن عصوك يا محمد في الأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says this truce-like instruction was abrogated by the sword verse.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا موادعة نسختها آية السيف
